text: We have to work very carefully because, as we all know, TACs differ very significantly.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Many of the TACs have adequately resourced secretariats already.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: What we need to do is to work with them to strategise and to work out the sectoral plan.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: This is the area where the secondment of the 20 public officers will make some impact.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Then we will have to see how it goes.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Based on the experience of working with these TACs, we will have to then amend and adapt our plans accordingly.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The Minister did talk about the benefits of TPP.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Clearly, quite a list of things that our businesses can benefit from.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We know that TPP is now political football, as we observe the US elections.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Given that we also have a US-Singapore FTA, with that FTA plus RCEP, without TPP, does it impact us that much?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I wish to hear the Minister's views on this.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We have all been following the progress of TPP in the various countries, all 12 of us.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: For the US, they have been telling us that they are very deeply engaged with the Congress leadership.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: They have very good experience taking the Trade Promotion Authority, the fast-track authority, through Congress.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: They know roughly where the votes lie – both in the House as well as the Senate.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: They are having very close links with the congressional leaders in the different groups to see whether this vote pool is still valid for the next step of ratification.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: I gave the examples of automotive components and textiles and garments.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Singapore companies can now source from TPP countries and this is then added on to qualify for the rules of origin to enter preferentially into the TPP markets.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: So, even though we may have the US-Singapore FTA, the TPP adds a new dimension and more market access.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Therefore, it is very important for us to have the TPP ratified as soon as possible so that our companies can benefit from the TPP.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: On the RCEP, it is a very different set of dynamics, because we have the ASEAN countries and the six ASEAN+1 dialogue partners.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As we know, with the dialogue partners – Australia, New Zealand, China, Japan, Korea and India – the dynamics are very complicated.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: For example, to get the RCEP resolved, you have to solve the bilateral dynamics between India and China, just to illustrate.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: So, it is not a simple task where we can get to a successful conclusion of RCEP by the end of the year.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We still need many, many more steps to get there.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As to the dynamics between TPP and RCEP, it is quite obvious that when TPP was concluded, there was greater pressure on RCEP participants to get RCEP also concluded.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: RCEP participants may not feel the same pressure to get it concluded.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: This is already in addition to the very complicated political dynamics within the 10+6 participants of RCEP.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Mr Chairman, since the TPP and RCEP are so complicated, are we looking at some other alternatives?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: China recently has announced "One Belt One Road" as a new macroeconomic strategy.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Is MTI looking into how Singapore can position itself to take advantage of the new economic strategy?

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We have a bilateral FTA which we are in the process of reviewing and improving.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We have an ASEAN-China FTA, which also presents quite a lot of additional benefits to us.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Last year, we just concluded an upgrade of the ASEAN-China FTA.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Over and above this, we have the RCEP.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The reason why I consider the RCEP very important is, as I had explained in my speech just now, in North America, you have NAFTA, and that makes it very difficult for us to break into NAFTA, because the supply chain of the US, Canada and Mexico is very closely integrated.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: So, when we have TPP, we are now able to be part of that bigger ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As I had mentioned, our automotive components companies now have a fair chance of breaking into the automotive market in the US and compete with Mexico and Canada.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: In Asia, there is a potential NAFTA-equivalent if China, Korea and Japan conclude their trilateral FTA.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: So, it is very important for us to have the RCEP, so that we are part of the 10+6, so that we are also part of a bigger market and a bigger ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As I had emphasised in my speech just now, our trade policy must be inclusionary.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We should not be left out, because we want market access to as many markets as possible.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
text: He mentioned that JTC has only 18% of the industrial space for rent and, therefore, does not have much influence over the rent of industrial space.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his clarifications.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As mentioned in my speech earlier, there will be 2.3 million square metres of industrial space that will come on stream annually in the next two years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think market forces would allow rentals to soften over the next couple of years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: With the supply of retail and industrial space coming up, I do not think we are in any position to add to the supply.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If there are no other clarifications, Mr Liang, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: In this year's Budget, clearly, the word "transformation" is key.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: It is mentioned so many times – as well as "industry transformation".

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: These are obviously the priority items in this year's Budget.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And thereafter, we will have the CFE where, again, MTI will be all hands on deck to push ahead with the transformation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Minister Iswaran mentioned about the formidable task ahead and we empathise with the responsibility on MTI's shoulders.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I just want to say that MTI and the family of agencies should draw on the inspiration of the power-packed Transformers, since they are transforming the economy, and then charge ahead.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, we wish you all the best and we are with you.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I want to thank Minister Lim, Minister Iswaran, Minister of State Koh Poh Koon and Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling for their replies.
